## 6. Harness, providers and models

Claude Code is the only harness, because it is the one whose own tools can all
be removed — and the machine it runs on holds the factory's secrets.
`harness.ADAPTERS` is the seam a general harness plugs into: a payload builder,
`<prefix>::start / status / stop`, and a declared `confinement`; only `strict`
may run.

The provider is a per-turn environment for the Claude Code process, built from
`PATH`, `HOME` and **one key — the requester's own** for that provider. The
Anthropic key is emptied whenever another endpoint is used.

| provider | how | key |
|---|---|---|
| `anthropic` (default) | the person's Claude account | their `claude setup-token` |
| `anthropic-api` | Console API key | theirs |
| `kimi`, `deepseek`, `zai`, `openrouter` | Anthropic-compatible endpoint | theirs; OpenRouter also reaches OpenAI models on their own account |
| `openai` | LiteLLM gateway on `127.0.0.1:4000`, translating to OpenAI (`llm-router` was the iii-first choice and serves no HTTP) | **shared**: one org `OPENAI_API_KEY` — passing a person's own key through the gateway is not proven |

## 7. Deploying it

| file | what |
|---|---|
| `deploy/Dockerfile` | node + python + pinned iii, sprite CLI, gh, Caddy, LiteLLM, and the claude-code worker built from `iii-hq/workers@954e787`. `iii project generate-docker` was tried first and targets the older single-config project shape |
| `deploy/fly.toml` | one machine, never auto-stopped (the reconciler must run), volume at `/data`, one public service on 8080 |
| `deploy/worker-compose.fly.yaml` | engine, state, http, mcp, cron, claude-code, sprite-worker, wipp-factory — every listener on 127.0.0.1. **No console**: it is the whole engine with a UI and cannot be bound to loopback, so on Fly it would be reachable from the Fly organization's private network |
| `deploy/config/` | Fly's values over the repository's generated `config/` — the configuration store wins over compose. The repository's `claude-code.yaml` pointed `claude_executable` at a temporary shim on the operator's laptop |
| `.dockerignore` | keeps `.env` and every local directory off Fly's builder |
| `deploy/Caddyfile` | `:8080`: `/wipp/*` → the app; `/` → `/wipp/`; everything else 404. `:8081`: the iii console, every request checked by the app first |
| `deploy/boundary.py` | the fail-closed listener check |
| `deploy/start.sh` | seeds settings onto the volume once; starts the gateway, compose and Caddy under one supervisor; refuses to start without its secrets |
| [`docs/deploy.md`](deploy.md) | the runbook |

**The factory's own secrets** — everything else is a person's, in the vault:

| secret | what |
|---|---|
| `SPRITES_TOKEN` | the sprites org |
| `WIPP_VAULT_KEY` | the Fernet key that opens the vault |
| `GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`, `GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` | the OAuth app people sign in with, owned by `parentoleave` |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` + `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` | optional, for the shared OpenAI gateway |

## 8. Keeping it safe

| # | layer | threat | control |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | edge | the internet | Fly TLS; Caddy is the only public listener |
| 2 | sign-in | anyone outside the org | GitHub OAuth with a one-time `state`; the token must belong to an **active** member of `parentoleave`; anything else — a pending invite, a revoked token, GitHub unreachable — is a refusal with no session |
| 3 | the list | an org member nobody granted anything | must also be on wipp's list; no sign-up |
| 4 | staying in | someone removed from the org | membership re-checked every 15 minutes; a failed check ends the session |
| 5 | sessions | stolen cookies, CSRF | random token, only its hash stored; `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/wipp`; every POST needs `X-Wipp: 1`; no header is trusted for identity |
| 6 | roles | doing more than granted | viewer / operator / admin, on every route; operators act on their own jobs |
| 7 | the proxy forwards `/wipp/*` only | anyone reaching `/mcp` — a shell in every sprite — or the engine | `deploy/Caddyfile`; asserted by `tests/test_deploy.py` |
| 8 | internal ports | going round the proxy, or another app in the Fly organization | engine, stream, http (and with it `/mcp`), console and gateway bind 127.0.0.1. **Fail closed:** `deploy/boundary.py` reads the kernel's own table of listening sockets — anything beyond loopback other than Caddy (8080, 8081) or Fly's SSH on its private network stops the machine. Caddy does not start until it passes, and it is re-checked every minute |
| 8a | the iii console | anyone but an admin reaching the whole engine | `https://wipp.fly.dev:8443` → Caddy `forward_auth` asks the app before **every** request, WebSocket included: no session → sign in; not admin → 403; app down or erroring → no response is 2xx, so nothing is forwarded. Access is audited |
| 9 | the vault | a copy of the volume | per-person secrets encrypted with `WIPP_VAULT_KEY`; shown back only as `…last4` |
| 10 | **credentials and sprites** | a turn leaving something behind — a hook, a credential helper, a `url.insteadOf` — that captures the next credential | the requester's token enters a sprite **once**, to clone, before any turn has run there, and is never written to disk; after the first turn the sprite is marked tainted and a clone is refused. The push happens on the factory: the sprite's commits come out as a git bundle (objects, no code), go into a throwaway repository with hooks disabled, are pushed as the requester, and the repository is deleted |
| 11 | turn confinement | a turn touching the Fly machine | every local tool removed; no host settings, plugins or MCP servers; the turn's process holds one provider key and nothing else from the machine's environment |
| 12 | untrusted input | instructions hidden in a Jira issue or the repository | the request is quoted as data under a heading that says so; no turn can merge, comment or reach the tracker; a person merges every PR |
| 13 | cost and abuse | runaway loops; one person starving the rest | turn caps per stage; bounded revisions per tier; per-person active (2) and daily (10) limits; a global cap under the sprites org's; admin **pause** |
| 14 | audit | not knowing who did what | append-only `audit.jsonl`: sign-ins and refusals, submits, answers, approvals, overrides, stops, destroys, settings edits, people added and removed |
| 15 | previews | a preview open to the world | public by decision, so it can be shared: the name carries 48 random bits, the sprite holds no credential at rest, every service runs inside the sprite on seed data — never shared staging — and the URL dies with the sprite |
| 16 | supply chain | a tool changing under us | every iii worker, CLI and binary pinned; asserted by `tests/test_deploy.py` |
| 17 | retention | data piling up | job records and evidence older than 30 days are pruned once their sprite is gone |

## 9. Lifetime

| event | sprite |
|---|---|
| PR open | up, as a preview; **extend** resets the idle clock |
| PR merged or closed | destroyed on the next reconcile |
| no activity for 72h | destroyed; the PR stays open; **revive** rebuilds it from the branch |
| failed or stopped, after 24h | destroyed |
| `wipp-j<12 hex>` with no job | destroyed — only that exact shape, so `wipp-demo`, `wipp-card-*` and every other sprite are never touched |

Admission refuses a job when the sprites org is at its running limit, and says so.

## 10. What is proven, and what is not

Proven by tests (`tests/test_factory.py`, `tests/test_deploy.py`; each safety
check was also confirmed to fail when the code under it was deliberately
broken): the whole stage machine from request to preview; every tier's
automatic fix and its bound; the identical-refusal stop; the ambiguity hatch in
fix turns; review blockers fixed once; screenshot-less proofs downgraded; CI
failures fixed on our commit and left alone on someone else's; teardown on merge
and the orphan rule; the push path for real (git bundle → throwaway repository →
a bare remote); inline setup of an unconfigured repository; the sprite taint;
per-turn key scoping; the vault's encryption; outsiders and unlisted members
refused; sessions ended on leaving the org; every API gate; the deploy boundary.

Not yet proven, in the order a first deploy will meet them:

1. **A deploy.** The image builds on Fly (817 MB). The first boot found the
   guessed `cron` version did not exist; it is now `0.21.25`, from the
   registry's own list.
2. **A real job through the new factory.** Phase 2 proved provisioning, the gate
   and a PR against parento-portal by hand; the stage machine has run only
   against stubs. The first job should be small and watched.
3. **Mutation testing on portal** (`required: false` until Infection's coverage
   driver is confirmed) and **`make metrics`** as a fair gate (`required: false`).
4. **The preview port forward** (`socat` to the sprite's URL port) for stacks not
   listening on 8080.
5. **Unauthenticated GitHub downloads during provisioning.** No credential is
   given to `prepare` (it runs while a turn may already be running). portal's
   one VCS dependency is public, so it works — but GitHub rate-limits anonymous
   API downloads per IP; watch the first few provisions.
6. **OpenAI through the gateway**: LiteLLM's Anthropic endpoint, with GPT models
   driving Claude Code's tool loop.

### Since this was written (2026-10-13)

Read from the commit history, **not re-confirmed against the running app**: a
commit message is evidence that something happened once, not that it holds now.
Each "shown" line names its commit. Confirm the rest on the next watched job.

| # | not yet proven, as listed above | what the history shows | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | a deploy | the first Fly boots and what they found: a cron version that did not exist (`bd69bfa`), a blank root and no settings (`79be793`), a sprites token of the wrong kind (`53e561e`), the console listening beyond loopback (`edbf45a`) | **shown** |
| 2 | a real job through the new factory | the first real job: setup racing the first turn (`f136a58`), a turn that never started and was waited on forever (`89c2f89`). The second: every turn failing on a Claude Code too old for the model (`34e6574`). Later work (merge, deploy watch, preview fixes) was done against real jobs | **shown** |
| 3 | mutation testing on portal; `make metrics` as a fair gate | Infection pinned to the release matching the project's php-parser (`2e7fe8d`), mutating only the lines a change touched, with time to run (`2190a0b`), and no silent exit on a missing folder (`79a7cca`). Nothing on `make metrics` | mutation **shown**; metrics **open** |
| 4 | the preview port forward | preview links pointing at the preview (`fb9fcc3`) and served over HTTPS at its own address (`4a7f7fb`); `preview.ready` run before every preview (`a9b415d`) | **shown** |
| 5 | anonymous GitHub downloads during provisioning | nothing either way | **open** |
| 6 | OpenAI through the LiteLLM gateway | nothing either way | **open** |

New since, and not yet proven on a real job (docs/completion-plan.md, Progress):

- **The gate** (`approval_gate: true`, `policy::check_permissions`). Proven by
  tests, and against the claude-code worker's source and the SDK's types, but no
  real turn has run through it yet. The first job after deploying it should be
  small and watched: a gate that denied everything would fail every turn
  closed, and one that allowed everything would look exactly like today.
- **The hook carrier.** Its runner assumes `python3` in the sprite. Sprites ship
  Python, but that is a fact about the image, not something a test here can see.
- **The console** is still out on Fly; the app now links to it only where
  `WIPP_CONSOLE_URL` is set.
# Deploying wipp to Fly

From nothing to a running factory at `https://wipp.fly.dev`, in the order the
steps depend on each other. The why behind each piece is in
[readiness-plan.md](readiness-plan.md); this is only the how.

## 1. The GitHub OAuth app (sign-in)

Create it **owned by the `parentoleave` organization**, not a person:
GitHub → `parentoleave` → Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps → New.

| field | value |
|---|---|
| Homepage URL | `https://wipp.fly.dev/wipp/` |
| Authorization callback URL | `https://wipp.fly.dev/wipp/auth/callback` |

Keep the client id and generate a client secret. If the org restricts
third-party application access, approve this app under
Settings → Third-party access, or members' tokens will not see org repositories.

## 2. The Fly app

```sh
fly apps create wipp --org <your-fly-org>
fly volumes create wipp_data --app wipp --region iad --size 20
```

## 3. Secrets

Only the factory's own. Everything a job runs as — GitHub, Claude, Jira, other
providers — is each person's, connected in the app.

```sh
fly secrets set --app wipp \
  SPRITES_TOKEN="REDACTED" \
  WIPP_VAULT_KEY="$(python3 -c 'from cryptography.fernet import Fernet; print(Fernet.generate_key().decode())')" \
  GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID="<from step 1>" \
  GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET="REDACTED"
```

`SPRITES_TOKEN` is a **sprites API token**, created at sprites.dev for the org
the sprites belong to, in the form `org-slug/org-id/token-id/token-value`. A
Fly token (`FlyV1 …`) is not one: the machine refuses to start with it.

**Keep a copy of `WIPP_VAULT_KEY`** somewhere safe (a password manager). Without
it the vault does not open, and everyone has to reconnect their accounts.

## 4. Deploy

From the repository root:

```sh
fly deploy --config deploy/fly.toml --dockerfile deploy/Dockerfile
fly logs --app wipp
```

The machine refuses to start, and says which, if a secret from step 3 is
missing. A healthy start logs `wipp-factory started — … routes under /wipp`.

If compose rejects a worker's version (`PACKAGE_NOT_RESOLVED`), the log lists
the versions that exist; pin one of those in `deploy/worker-compose.fly.yaml`
and deploy again.

## 5. First sign-in

Open `https://wipp.fly.dev/` → **Sign in with GitHub**. `ianparo` is an admin
from `settings/factory.yaml`; nobody else is on the list yet.

Then **Accounts** → **Claude**: on your own machine, once —

```sh
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash   # if Claude Code is not installed
claude setup-token                               # sign in in the browser it opens
```

— and paste the token it prints. That is everything a first request needs.

## 6. Adding people

**Settings → People → Add a person**, by GitHub login, with a role:

| role | may |
|---|---|
| viewer | see jobs, evidence, previews and pull requests |
| operator | + submit requests, answer questions, approve plans, stop their own jobs |
| admin | + people, settings, repository proposals, destroy any environment, pause intake, the audit log |

They must be an active member of `parentoleave` as well; anyone else gets no
access at all. Removing someone from the org ends their access within fifteen
minutes.

## 7. Day to day

| want to | do |
|---|---|
| stop new work | Settings → **Pause intake** |
| see who did what | **Audit** |
| make a drafted repository setup permanent | Settings → **Repository settings drafted by jobs** → Make permanent |
| change a phase's default model, limits, a repository's guardrails | Settings → settings files (validated, backed up, audited) |
| list wipp's sprites | `fly ssh console --app wipp -C "sprite list"` |

## 8. Running it locally

```sh
make install
cp .env.example .env    # then fill in the GitHub OAuth app for localhost (below)
make up                 # engine + workers, including wipp-factory
open http://127.0.0.1:3121/wipp/
```

Local sign-in needs its own OAuth app with callback
`http://127.0.0.1:3121/wipp/auth/callback`, and `WIPP_PUBLIC_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3121`
in `.env`. The vault key is generated beside the local data.
# Deferred

*2026-10-16. What was set aside, and why, so it is not lost. The end-goal plan
that held these (G1–G9, S1, A1–A2, C1, L1–L2, H1–H2, K1, V1, E1) is done and
dropped; it is in git history at `docs/end-goal-plan.md`. Each item below says
what would bring it forward.*

## Waiting on a decision or on something outside wipp

- **A second trusted server through `rbac-proxy`** (iii-native proposal P2):
  `rbac-proxy` as the engine's one public listener, each server with its own
  credential scoped to its functions. Deferred by decision (2026-10-14).
- **Private previews.** Each ephemeral environment open only to members of the
  org, enforced by the sprites platform:
  - `sprite config update --url-auth sprite --private-access org_users` in
    place of today's `--auth public`, failing closed: a preview that cannot be
    made private is not served;
  - the prove turn reaches the app from inside the sprite at its local port,
    because a turn has no org token and must not get one. The app's own links
    point at the preview address, so the brief tells the turn to rewrite those
    onto the local port with Playwright's request routing.

  People then open a preview signed in to the org. Brought forward if people
  beyond the team use wipp, or a preview ever holds more than test data.
- **Staging and demo as UAT places**, once those environments exist. The merge
  already deploys to staging and the job watches that deploy; UAT itself stays
  the requester's sign-off in the preview, before the merge.
- **Sprite startup** (proposal §7a): cached Docker layers in a registry, plus
  the warm pool. Needs a registry chosen.
- **More than one warm sprite per repository** (2026-10-22). The pool keeps
  exactly one prepared sprite per repository with `warm: true`
  (`workers/wipp-factory/src/warm.py`), so when jobs run in parallel only the
  first skips the ~7 minutes of setup. Make `warm:` take a number (`warm: 2`)
  and keep that many ready per repository; keep the total across repositories,
  plus `max_jobs`, under the sprites org's running limit (10). Each warm sprite
  is an idle sprite paid for. Brought forward when a second repository is
  onboarded with its own warm sprite, or when parallel jobs on one repository
  become routine.

## Quality gates

- **Mutation testing as a gate on the portal.** It runs and does not block.
  On the second real job (ja8e5899097e8) the cause showed: Stryker's Vitest
  runner crashes on start (`Cannot destructure property 'moduleGraph' of
  'project.server'`), a version mismatch between `@stryker-mutator/vitest-runner`
  and the portal's Vitest, not the change under test. The PHP side's suspected
  missing coverage driver is unconfirmed. Fix both in the portal before making
  it required.

## The record

- **The audit log stays JSONL; a SQLite index for questions, if reads get
  slow** (2026-10-13). The record is `audit-log`'s sealed, hash-chained JSONL
  files: append-only by nature, readable and verifiable with nothing but a text
  tool, shippable as they are to the storage service the anchor moves to.
  Since 2026-10-14 `audit-log` filters and pages itself, every reply capped in
  bytes. If the questions the app and an auditor ask (by job, kind, constraint,
  person and time) outgrow a full read inside `audit-log`, a SQLite index is
  built from the record by a subscriber to `audit::recorded`: disposable,
  rebuildable from the chain at any time, never authoritative, never what
  verification reads.

## Clean-up

- **The deletion** (proposal P4): the old `factory-worker`, `harness-core` and
  `policy-worker`, `claude-code/` and `repos.toml`, with this repository's own
  guardrails first moved onto `constraints.py`. They are the last places that
  name the operator's laptop (`/Users/tacoda/…`); none of them ships.

## Small follow-ups, found on the first two real jobs

- **Proof counts criteria twice** ("8 of 16" for 8): the request's criteria
  and each task's done-when lines are counted together. (In the UI plan, U5.)
- **An empty learn says nothing.** The learn turn on ja8e5899097e8 answered
  `{"proposals": []}` with no reason. Its brief should ask for one line per
  piece of evidence: why it is, or is not, a lesson.
- **A turn's thinking is not recorded.** Claude Code sends it only when asked;
  wipp-harness should ask, so the turn page (V1) shows it.
- **A turn could write a git hook** that runs when the factory commits at ship,
  inside the sprite, after the checks passed. Commit with hooks off and run the
  repository's own pre-commit from a clean copy.
- **Backups.** Every job, setting and the audit record live on one Fly volume.
  Confirm daily snapshots are on and that one restores. The Fly host reboot of
  2026-10-16 took wipp down for seven minutes and lost nothing; a host that
  never came back would take the volume with it.
- **`spikes/p0`** drives wipp-harness and has not been run since H1.
- **Vite** warns `inlineDynamicImports` is deprecated: use `codeSplitting: false`.
- **One audit entry is filed under `settings_saved`**, not `settings`: the
  first preview fix, made by hand. The record is append-only, so it stays.

| `deploy/config/` | Fly's values over the repository's generated `config/` — the configuration store wins over compose. The repository's `claude-code.yaml` pointed `claude_executable` at a temporary shim on the operator's laptop |
| `.dockerignore` | keeps `.env` and every local directory off Fly's builder |
| `deploy/Caddyfile` | `:8080`: `/wipp/*` → the app; `/` → `/wipp/`; everything else 404. `:8081`: the iii console, every request checked by the app first |
| `deploy/boundary.py` | the fail-closed listener check |
| `deploy/start.sh` | seeds settings onto the volume once; starts the gateway, compose and Caddy under one supervisor; refuses to start without its secrets |
| [`docs/deploy.md`](deploy.md) | the runbook |

**The factory's own secrets** — everything else is a person's, in the vault:

| secret | what |
|---|---|
| `SPRITES_TOKEN` | the sprites org |
| `WIPP_VAULT_KEY` | the Fernet key that opens the vault |
| `GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`, `GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` | the OAuth app people sign in with, owned by `parentoleave` |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` + `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` | optional, for the shared OpenAI gateway |

## 8. Keeping it safe

| # | layer | threat | control |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | edge | the internet | Fly TLS; Caddy is the only public listener |
| 2 | sign-in | anyone outside the org | GitHub OAuth with a one-time `state`; the token must belong to an **active** member of `parentoleave`; anything else — a pending invite, a revoked token, GitHub unreachable — is a refusal with no session |
| 3 | the list | an org member nobody granted anything | must also be on wipp's list; no sign-up |
| 4 | staying in | someone removed from the org | membership re-checked every 15 minutes; a failed check ends the session |
| 5 | sessions | stolen cookies, CSRF | random token, only its hash stored; `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/wipp`; every POST needs `X-Wipp: 1`; no header is trusted for identity |
| 6 | roles | doing more than granted | viewer / operator / admin, on every route; operators act on their own jobs |
| 7 | the proxy forwards `/wipp/*` only | anyone reaching `/mcp` — a shell in every sprite — or the engine | `deploy/Caddyfile`; asserted by `tests/test_deploy.py` |
| 8 | internal ports | going round the proxy, or another app in the Fly organization | engine, stream, http (and with it `/mcp`), console and gateway bind 127.0.0.1. **Fail closed:** `deploy/boundary.py` reads the kernel's own table of listening sockets — anything beyond loopback other than Caddy (8080, 8081) or Fly's SSH on its private network stops the machine. Caddy does not start until it passes, and it is re-checked every minute |
| 8a | the iii console | anyone but an admin reaching the whole engine | `https://wipp.fly.dev:8443` → Caddy `forward_auth` asks the app before **every** request, WebSocket included: no session → sign in; not admin → 403; app down or erroring → no response is 2xx, so nothing is forwarded. Access is audited |
| 9 | the vault | a copy of the volume | per-person secrets encrypted with `WIPP_VAULT_KEY`; shown back only as `…last4` |
| 10 | **credentials and sprites** | a turn leaving something behind — a hook, a credential helper, a `url.insteadOf` — that captures the next credential | the requester's token enters a sprite **once**, to clone, before any turn has run there, and is never written to disk; after the first turn the sprite is marked tainted and a clone is refused. The push happens on the factory: the sprite's commits come out as a git bundle (objects, no code), go into a throwaway repository with hooks disabled, are pushed as the requester, and the repository is deleted |
| 11 | turn confinement | a turn touching the Fly machine | every local tool removed; no host settings, plugins or MCP servers; the turn's process holds one provider key and nothing else from the machine's environment |
| 12 | untrusted input | instructions hidden in a Jira issue or the repository | the request is quoted as data under a heading that says so; no turn can merge, comment or reach the tracker; a person merges every PR |
| 13 | cost and abuse | runaway loops; one person starving the rest | turn caps per stage; bounded revisions per tier; per-person active (2) and daily (10) limits; a global cap under the sprites org's; admin **pause** |
| 14 | audit | not knowing who did what | append-only `audit.jsonl`: sign-ins and refusals, submits, answers, approvals, overrides, stops, destroys, settings edits, people added and removed |
| 15 | previews | a preview open to the world | public by decision, so it can be shared: the name carries 48 random bits, the sprite holds no credential at rest, every service runs inside the sprite on seed data — never shared staging — and the URL dies with the sprite |
| 16 | supply chain | a tool changing under us | every iii worker, CLI and binary pinned; asserted by `tests/test_deploy.py` |
| 17 | retention | data piling up | job records and evidence older than 30 days are pruned once their sprite is gone |

## 9. Lifetime

| event | sprite |
|---|---|
| PR open | up, as a preview; **extend** resets the idle clock |
| PR merged or closed | destroyed on the next reconcile |
| no activity for 72h | destroyed; the PR stays open; **revive** rebuilds it from the branch |
| failed or stopped, after 24h | destroyed |
| `wipp-j<12 hex>` with no job | destroyed — only that exact shape, so `wipp-demo`, `wipp-card-*` and every other sprite are never touched |

Admission refuses a job when the sprites org is at its running limit, and says so.

## 10. What is proven, and what is not

Proven by tests (`tests/test_factory.py`, `tests/test_deploy.py`; each safety
check was also confirmed to fail when the code under it was deliberately
broken): the whole stage machine from request to preview; every tier's
automatic fix and its bound; the identical-refusal stop; the ambiguity hatch in
fix turns; review blockers fixed once; screenshot-less proofs downgraded; CI
failures fixed on our commit and left alone on someone else's; teardown on merge
and the orphan rule; the push path for real (git bundle → throwaway repository →
a bare remote); inline setup of an unconfigured repository; the sprite taint;
per-turn key scoping; the vault's encryption; outsiders and unlisted members
refused; sessions ended on leaving the org; every API gate; the deploy boundary.

Not yet proven, in the order a first deploy will meet them:

1. **A deploy.** The image builds on Fly (817 MB). The first boot found the
   guessed `cron` version did not exist; it is now `0.21.25`, from the
   registry's own list.
2. **A real job through the new factory.** Phase 2 proved provisioning, the gate
   and a PR against parento-portal by hand; the stage machine has run only
   against stubs. The first job should be small and watched.
3. **Mutation testing on portal** (`required: false` until Infection's coverage
   driver is confirmed) and **`make metrics`** as a fair gate (`required: false`).
4. **The preview port forward** (`socat` to the sprite's URL port) for stacks not
   listening on 8080.
5. **Unauthenticated GitHub downloads during provisioning.** No credential is
   given to `prepare` (it runs while a turn may already be running). portal's
   one VCS dependency is public, so it works — but GitHub rate-limits anonymous
   API downloads per IP; watch the first few provisions.
6. **OpenAI through the gateway**: LiteLLM's Anthropic endpoint, with GPT models
   driving Claude Code's tool loop.

### Since this was written (2026-10-13)

Read from the commit history, **not re-confirmed against the running app**: a
commit message is evidence that something happened once, not that it holds now.
Each "shown" line names its commit. Confirm the rest on the next watched job.

| # | not yet proven, as listed above | what the history shows | status |

| 1 | a deploy | the first Fly boots and what they found: a cron version that did not exist (`bd69bfa`), a blank root and no settings (`79be793`), a sprites token of the wrong kind (`53e561e`), the console listening beyond loopback (`edbf45a`) | **shown** |

The second: every turn failing on a Claude Code too old for the model (`34e6574`). Later work (merge, deploy watch, preview fixes) was done against real jobs | **shown** |
| 3 | mutation testing on portal; `make metrics` as a fair gate | Infection pinned to the release matching the project's php-parser (`2e7fe8d`), mutating only the lines a change touched, with time to run (`2190a0b`), and no silent exit on a missing folder (`79a7cca`). Nothing on `make metrics` | mutation **shown**; metrics **open** |
| 4 | the preview port forward | preview links pointing at the preview (`fb9fcc3`) and served over HTTPS at its own address (`4a7f7fb`); `preview.ready` run before every preview (`a9b415d`) | **shown** |

| 6 | OpenAI through the LiteLLM gateway | nothing either way | **open** |

New since, and not yet proven on a real job (docs/completion-plan.md, Progress):

- **The gate** (`approval_gate: true`, `policy::check_permissions`). Proven by

# Deploying wipp to Fly

From nothing to a running factory at `https://wipp.fly.dev`, in the order the
steps depend on each other. The why behind each piece is in
[readiness-plan.md](readiness-plan.md); this is only the how.

## 1. The GitHub OAuth app (sign-in)

Create it **owned by the `parentoleave` organization**, not a person:
GitHub → `parentoleave` → Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps → New.

| field | value |
|---|---|
| Homepage URL | `https://wipp.fly.dev/wipp/` |
| Authorization callback URL | `https://wipp.fly.dev/wipp/auth/callback` |

Keep the client id and generate a client secret. If the org restricts
third-party application access, approve this app under
Settings → Third-party access, or members' tokens will not see org repositories.

## 2. The Fly app

```sh
fly apps create wipp --org <your-fly-org>
fly volumes create wipp_data --app wipp --region iad --size 20
```

## 3. Secrets

Only the factory's own. Everything a job runs as — GitHub, Claude, Jira, other
providers — is each person's, connected in the app.

```sh
fly secrets set --app wipp \
  SPRITES_TOKEN="REDACTED" \
  WIPP_VAULT_KEY="$(python3 -c 'from cryptography.fernet import Fernet; print(Fernet.generate_key().decode())')" \
  GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID="<from step 1>" \
  GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET="REDACTED"
```

`SPRITES_TOKEN` is a **sprites API token**, created at sprites.dev for the org
the sprites belong to, in the form `org-slug/org-id/token-id/token-value`. A
Fly token (`FlyV1 …`) is not one: the machine refuses to start with it.

**Keep a copy of `WIPP_VAULT_KEY`** somewhere safe (a password manager). Without
it the vault does not open, and everyone has to reconnect their accounts.

## 4. Deploy

From the repository root:

```sh
fly deploy --config deploy/fly.toml --dockerfile deploy/Dockerfile
fly logs --app wipp
```

The machine refuses to start, and says which, if a secret from step 3 is
missing. A healthy start logs `wipp-factory started — … routes under /wipp`.

If compose rejects a worker's version (`PACKAGE_NOT_RESOLVED`), the log lists
the versions that exist; pin one of those in `deploy/worker-compose.fly.yaml`
and deploy again.

## 5. First sign-in

Open `https://wipp.fly.dev/` → **Sign in with GitHub**. `ianparo` is an admin
from `settings/factory.yaml`; nobody else is on the list yet.

Then **Accounts** → **Claude**: on your own machine, once —

```sh
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash   # if Claude Code is not installed
claude setup-token                               # sign in in the browser it opens
```

— and paste the token it prints. That is everything a first request needs.

## 6. Adding people

**Settings → People → Add a person**, by GitHub login, with a role:

| role | may |
|---|---|
| viewer | see jobs, evidence, previews and pull requests |
| operator | + submit requests, answer questions, approve plans, stop their own jobs |
| admin | + people, settings, repository proposals, destroy any environment, pause intake, the audit log |

They must be an active member of `parentoleave` as well; anyone else gets no
access at all. Removing someone from the org ends their access within fifteen
minutes.

## 7. Day to day

| want to | do |
|---|---|
| stop new work | Settings → **Pause intake** |
| see who did what | **Audit** |
| make a drafted repository setup permanent | Settings → **Repository settings drafted by jobs** → Make permanent |
| change a phase's default model, limits, a repository's guardrails | Settings → settings files (validated, backed up, audited) |
| list wipp's sprites | `fly ssh console --app wipp -C "sprite list"` |

## 8. Running it locally

```sh
make install
cp .env.example .env    # then fill in the GitHub OAuth app for localhost (below)
make up                 # engine + workers, including wipp-factory
open http://127.0.0.1:3121/wipp/
```

Local sign-in needs its own OAuth app with callback
`http://127.0.0.1:3121/wipp/auth/callback`, and `WIPP_PUBLIC_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3121`
in `.env`. The vault key is generated beside the local data.
# Deferred

*2026-10-16. What was set aside, and why, so it is not lost. The end-goal plan
that held these (G1–G9, S1, A1–A2, C1, L1–L2, H1–H2, K1, V1, E1) is done and
dropped; it is in git history at `docs/end-goal-plan.md`. Each item below says
what would bring it forward.*

## Waiting on a decision or on something outside wipp

- **A second trusted server through `rbac-proxy`** (iii-native proposal P2):
  `rbac-proxy` as the engine's one public listener, each server with its own
  credential scoped to its functions. Deferred by decision (2026-10-14).
- **Private previews.** Each ephemeral environment open only to members of the
  org, enforced by the sprites platform:
  - `sprite config update --url-auth sprite --private-access org_users` in
    place of today's `--auth public`, failing closed: a preview that cannot be
    made private is not served;
  - the prove turn reaches the app from inside the sprite at its local port,
    because a turn has no org token and must not get one. The app's own links
    point at the preview address, so the brief tells the turn to rewrite those
    onto the local port with Playwright's request routing.

  People then open a preview signed in to the org. Brought forward if people
  beyond the team use wipp, or a preview ever holds more than test data.
- **Staging and demo as UAT places**, once those environments exist. The merge
  already deploys to staging and the job watches that deploy; UAT itself stays
  the requester's sign-off in the preview, before the merge.
- **Sprite startup** (proposal §7a): cached Docker layers in a registry, plus
  the warm pool. Needs a registry chosen.
- **More than one warm sprite per repository** (2026-10-22). The pool keeps
  exactly one prepared sprite per repository with `warm: true`
  (`workers/wipp-factory/src/warm.py`), so when jobs run in parallel only the
  first skips the ~7 minutes of setup. Make `warm:` take a number (`warm: 2`)
  and keep that many ready per repository; keep the total across repositories,
  plus `max_jobs`, under the sprites org's running limit (10). Each warm sprite
  is an idle sprite paid for. Brought forward when a second repository is
  onboarded with its own warm sprite, or when parallel jobs on one repository
  become routine.

## Quality gates

- **Mutation testing as a gate on the portal.** It runs and does not block.
  On the second real job (ja8e5899097e8) the cause showed: Stryker's Vitest
  runner crashes on start (`Cannot destructure property 'moduleGraph' of
  'project.server'`), a version mismatch between `@stryker-mutator/vitest-runner`
  and the portal's Vitest, not the change under test. The PHP side's suspected
  missing coverage driver is unconfirmed. Fix both in the portal before making
  it required.

## The record

- **The audit log stays JSONL; a SQLite index for questions, if reads get
  slow** (2026-10-13). The record is `audit-log`'s sealed, hash-chained JSONL
  files: append-only by nature, readable and verifiable with nothing but a text
  tool, shippable as they are to the storage service the anchor moves to.
  Since 2026-10-14 `audit-log` filters and pages itself, every reply capped in
  bytes. If the questions the app and an auditor ask (by job, kind, constraint,
  person and time) outgrow a full read inside `audit-log`, a SQLite index is
  built from the record by a subscriber to `audit::recorded`: disposable,
  rebuildable from the chain at any time, never authoritative, never what
  verification reads.

## Clean-up

- **The deletion** (proposal P4): the old `factory-worker`, `harness-core` and
  `policy-worker`, `claude-code/` and `repos.toml`, with this repository's own
  guardrails first moved onto `constraints.py`. They are the last places that
  name the operator's laptop (`/Users/tacoda/…`); none of them ships.

## Small follow-ups, found on the first two real jobs

- **Proof counts criteria twice** ("8 of 16" for 8): the request's criteria
  and each task's done-when lines are counted together. (In the UI plan, U5.)
- **An empty learn says nothing.** The learn turn on ja8e5899097e8 answered
  `{"proposals": []}` with no reason. Its brief should ask for one line per
  piece of evidence: why it is, or is not, a lesson.
- **A turn's thinking is not recorded.** Claude Code sends it only when asked;
  wipp-harness should ask, so the turn page (V1) shows it.
- **A turn could write a git hook** that runs when the factory commits at ship,
  inside the sprite, after the checks passed. Commit with hooks off and run the
  repository's own pre-commit from a clean copy.
- **Backups.** Every job, setting and the audit record live on one Fly volume.
  Confirm daily snapshots are on and that one restores. The Fly host reboot of
  2026-10-16 took wipp down for seven minutes and lost nothing; a host that
  never came back would take the volume with it.
- **`spikes/p0`** drives wipp-harness and has not been run since H1.
- **Vite** warns `inlineDynamicImports` is deprecated: use `codeSplitting: false`.
- **One audit entry is filed under `settings_saved`**, not `settings`: the
  first preview fix, made by hand. The record is append-only, so it stays.

import config
import constraints
import evals
import forge
import gate
import harness
import learn
import parse
import request_form
import sandbox
import backtest
import sprite_runtime
import oversight
import escapes
import models
import store
import warm

# `queued`: admitted, waiting for room to start (G6).
# `blocked`: a part of a split, waiting for the parts it follows to land.
# `split`: a request decomposed into parts; it tracks them and lands with them.
ACTIVE = ("queued", "ready", "running", "turn", "needs_you", "waiting", "blocked", "split")
FINISHED = ("landed", "closed", "failed", "stopped")
TURN_STAGES = ("scope", "discover", "plan", "define", "specify", "falsify", "implement", "refactor", "review",
               "prove",
               "comprehend", "ci_fix", "onboard",
               "learn", "grade")
# The turns asked to say what surprised them (briefs.SURPRISES): what the
# factory did not know, for learn.
SURPRISING = ("specify", "implement", "prove")
ORPHAN = re.compile(r"^wipp-j[0-9a-f]{12}$")


# A quality tool's exit code for "the measurement is broken, not the code".
TOOL_BROKEN = 2
TRANSIENT_TRIES = 3
# G9.3: each job's steps run as messages on iii's queue, one job's in order
# (FIFO, grouped by job) and different jobs' side by side. Persisted by the
# queue worker on the volume, redelivered after an engine restart, and seen
# by iii (depth, failures, dead letters). A stage can run for a long time
# (checks, quality), hence two hours rather than the queue's thirty minutes.
STAGE_QUEUE = "wipp-stages"
STAGE_QUEUE_CONFIG = {"type": "fifo", "message_group_field": "job_id", "concurrency": 20, "max_retries": 2,
                      "backoff_ms": 1000, "poll_interval_ms": 100, "redeliver_on_engine_restart": True,
                      "timeout_ms": 7_200_000}
# How long `dispatched` trusts a queued step: the queue's own timeout, after
# which it delivers the step again itself, or has lost it.
DISPATCH_TRUSTED_S = STAGE_QUEUE_CONFIG["timeout_ms"] / 1000 + 300
# A turn still live this long is stopped and treated as one that did not reply
# (a retry, then a person). Without a limit, a harness that never ended its turn
# kept the job in `turn` for ever, polled and left alone (progress.qnt,
# `noTurnLimit`). A stage's block may say `max_minutes`.
TURN_MINUTES = 120
# "session not found": the exec session dropped before the command started
# (j862122f69c8b, in its checks). Not "sprite not found": a sprite that is gone
# does not come back on a retry.
TRANSIENT_SIGNS = ("connection to exec session", "was lost", "i/o timeout", "connection reset",
                   "connection refused", "timed out waiting", "session not found")


# The engine between a function and its worker: a worker restarting (a deploy)
# has unregistered its functions for a few seconds, or a call was cut off.
# Nothing about the job, and nothing a person needs to decide.
ENGINE_SIGNS = ("function_not_found", "not found in namespace", "invocation_stopped", "invocation timed out")
ENGINE_TRIES = 12


def engine_blip(exc: Exception) -> bool:
    text = str(exc).lower()
    return any(sign in text for sign in ENGINE_SIGNS)


def transient(exc: Exception) -> bool:
    """A failure of the connection to a sprite, not of anything run in it."""
    text = str(exc).lower()
    return type(exc).__name__ == "Unavailable" and any(sign in text for sign in TRANSIENT_SIGNS)


def read_only(granted: list[str]) -> bool:
    """A turn that can run commands and was not given the editor."""
    return any(t.endswith("sprite__exec") for t in granted) and not any(t.endswith("sprite__code__write")
                                                                     for t in granted)

class Refused(Exception):
    """A request the factory will not accept. Its message is the app's message."""


class Factory:
    def __init__(self, trigger):
        self.trigger = trigger
        self.threads: dict[str, threading.Thread] = {}
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
        # How a step is run: through iii's queue once factory.py sets this
        # (`trigger`), and on a thread here otherwise (tests, no engine).
        self.enqueue = None
        # Each job with a step queued, and when (docs/models/progress.qnt). An
        # entry older than the queue's own timeout is not trusted: its message
        # was lost, or the queue is delivering it again itself.
        self.dispatched: dict[str, float] = {}
        # Each job with a step being consumed right now: a second message for it
        # (the queue's redelivery of a step that outlasted its timeout) does nothing.
        self.handling: set[str] = set()
        self.last_reconcile = 0.0
        self.pool = warm.Pool(self)
        # The stage machine, in one place: what the factory does on reaching a
        # stage, and what it does with a turn's reply. `clarify`, `approve` and
        # `preview` have no action — a person, or GitHub, moves them on.
        self.actions = {
            "provision": self.do_provision, "prepare": lambda job: self.move(job, "scope"),
            "onboard": self.do_onboard, "scope": self.do_scope,
            "discover": self.do_discover, "plan": self.do_plan, "define": self.do_define, "specify": self.do_specify,
            "baseline": self.do_baseline, "verify": self.do_verify, "strengthened": self.do_strengthened,
            "implement": self.do_implement,
            "checks": self.do_checks, "review": self.do_review,
            "ci_fix": self.do_ci_fix, "acceptance": self.do_acceptance,
            # Waiting on the pull request's CI: the reconciler moves it on.
            "ci": lambda job: self.move(job, "ci", "waiting"),
            # Steps that wait on a person, asked again if a retry lands on them.
            "your_checks": self.ask_definitions,
            "refactor": self.do_refactor, "falsify": self.do_falsify,
            "prove": self.do_prove, "comprehend": self.do_comprehend, "ship": self.do_ship, "uat": self.do_uat,
            "revive": self.do_revive, "deploy": self.do_deploy, "learn": self.do_learn,
            "eval_checks": self.do_eval_checks, "grade": self.do_grade, "backtest": self.do_backtest,
        }
        self.results = {
            "onboard": self.after_onboard, "scope": self.after_scope, "discover": self.after_discover,
            "plan": self.after_plan, "define": self.after_define, "specify": self.after_specify,
            "implement": self.after_implement, "review": self.after_review, "prove": self.after_prove,
            "comprehend": self.after_comprehend, "learn": self.after_learn, "refactor": self.after_refactor,
            "falsify": self.after_falsify,
            "ci_fix": self.after_ci_fix,
        }

    # --- intake ---

    def submit(self, actor: str, repo_name: str, text: str, extra: dict | None = None) -> dict:
        """Admit one request. `extra` may carry `overrides` (model choices),
        `title`, and `details` (request_form: kind, criteria, links, screenshots)."""
        extra = extra or {}
        details = request_form.clean(extra.get("details"))
        if store.flag("paused"):
"""The lifecycle of a constraint: proposed, told, observed, enforced, re-carried,
retired. Every change goes through here, from the app or the terminal.

A constraint's file says where it starts. Its placement in
`settings/constraints.yaml` says where it is now, and carries the history of
every change: who made it, why, and what it was before. That history is the
answer to "why is this carried the way it is", and the factory's records of
what each constraint did to real jobs (`evidence`) are the case for the next
change.

The checks below are the old factory's (`scripts/lifecycle.py`), restated for
carriers. Each refusal says what would make the change possible, because a
lifecycle that only said no would send people to edit the YAML by hand, past
every check here.
"""

import re

import yaml

import config
import constraints as C
import store

VERBS = ("tell", "observe", "enforce", "carry", "drop", "move", "set_policy",
         "overridable", "retire", "restore")

SUGGEST_ALLOWED_AFTER = 3        # allow-once grants before relaxing is suggested
SUGGEST_ENFORCE_AFTER = 5        # would-have-refused events before enforcing is suggested
SILENT_DAYS = 90


class Refused(ValueError):
    """A lifecycle change that would leave a constraint looking enforced and
    refusing nothing, or one nobody may make from here. The message says why."""


# --- reading and writing placement ---

def placement_file():
    return config.SETTINGS / "constraints.yaml"


def read_placements() -> dict:
    return C.placements()


def write_placements(entries: dict, actor: str, what: str) -> None:
    path = placement_file()
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if path.is_file():
        path.with_suffix(f".yaml.{int(store.now())}.bak").write_text(path.read_text())
    header = ("# Where each constraint is carried now. Written by the lifecycle (the\n"
              "# app's Constraints page, or scripts/lifecycle.py), never by hand: a hand\n"
              "# edit skips every check that keeps a constraint from looking enforced\n"
              "# while refusing nothing. See workers/wipp-factory/src/lifecycle.py.\n")
    path.write_text(header + yaml.safe_dump({"constraints": entries}, sort_keys=True, allow_unicode=True))
    store.audit(actor, "constraint", **{"change": what})

"""The lifecycle of a constraint: proposed, told, observed, enforced, re-carried,
retired. Every change goes through here, from the app or the terminal.

A constraint's file says where it starts. Its placement in
`settings/constraints.yaml` says where it is now, and carries the history of
every change: who made it, why, and what it was before. That history is the
answer to "why is this carried the way it is", and the factory's records of
what each constraint did to real jobs (`evidence`) are the case for the next
change.

The checks below are the old factory's (`scripts/lifecycle.py`), restated for
carriers. Each refusal says what would make the change possible, because a
lifecycle that only said no would send people to edit the YAML by hand, past
every check here.
"""

import re

import yaml

import config
import constraints as C
import store

VERBS = ("tell", "observe", "enforce", "carry", "drop", "move", "set_policy",
         "overridable", "retire", "restore")

SUGGEST_ALLOWED_AFTER = 3        # allow-once grants before relaxing is suggested
SUGGEST_ENFORCE_AFTER = 5        # would-have-refused events before enforcing is suggested
SILENT_DAYS = 90


class Refused(ValueError):
    """A lifecycle change that would leave a constraint looking enforced and
    refusing nothing, or one nobody may make from here. The message says why."""


# --- reading and writing placement ---

def placement_file():
    return config.SETTINGS / "constraints.yaml"


def read_placements() -> dict:
    return C.placements()


def write_placements(entries: dict, actor: str, what: str) -> None:
    path = placement_file()
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if path.is_file():
        path.with_suffix(f".yaml.{int(store.now())}.bak").write_text(path.read_text())
    header = ("# Where each constraint is carried now. Written by the lifecycle (the\n"
              "# app's Constraints page, or scripts/lifecycle.py), never by hand: a hand\n"
              "# edit skips every check that keeps a constraint from looking enforced\n"
              "# while refusing nothing. See workers/wipp-factory/src/lifecycle.py.\n")
    path.write_text(header + yaml.safe_dump({"constraints": entries}, sort_keys=True, allow_unicode=True))
    store.audit(actor, "constraint", **{"change": what})

"""The factory's records, their logs, and the audit trail.

Records (jobs, constraint snapshots, setup status, turn sessions, proposals,
the warm pool) are kept by `records`: in iii's `state` worker when the factory
runs (G9.1, switched on by `use_state` at boot), or in files with no engine.
`state` was rejected once, when its predecessor lost a live job on a restart;
spikes/p3/state_durability.py measured the worker this uses before anything
moved, and its store is on the volume, flushed every 100 ms.

A job's constraint snapshot is kept apart from the job: it is most of the
record (285 KB of 369 on the first real job), it is fixed once the repository's
own rules are read, and every tick lists every job. `load` puts it back;
`all_jobs` leaves it out.

Each job's activity log and its constraint events are appended to `state` as
well (G9.2). The audit log is append-only JSON lines and is never rewritten — not by
the reaper, not by retention. It is the answer to "who asked for this".
"""

import json
import os
import secrets
import threading
import time
from pathlib import Path

import audit_client
import records

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
DATA = Path(os.environ.get("WIPP_DATA", ROOT / "state" / "factory"))

_lock = threading.Lock()
# Files until the factory boots on the engine (`use_state`).
backend = records.Files(DATA)
# Each job's constraint snapshot as last read or written here: the factory is
# its only writer, so this is never stale, and a session reads it on every call.
_snapshots: dict[str, list] = {}


def use(chosen) -> None:
    global backend
    backend = chosen
    _snapshots.clear()


def use_state(trigger) -> dict:
    """Keep every record in iii's `state`, importing the old files first.
    Raises if `state` cannot be reached: a factory that silently fell back to
    files would split its records in two."""
    chosen = records.State(trigger)
    chosen.keys("jobs")
    use(chosen)
    return records.import_legacy(chosen, DATA)


def save(job: dict) -> dict:
    """Write the job, unless it was written since this copy was read. Its
    constraint snapshot, if it carries one, is written apart, and only when it
    changed.

    Every write bumps `rev`, and a copy whose `rev` is not the stored one is
    refused (`Stale`). Without it the last writer won: a step that had read the
    job before a person pressed Stop wrote its copy back minutes later, and the
    job went on (docs/models/lifecycle.qnt, the `stopSticks` counterexample).
    """
    with _lock:
        stored = backend.get("jobs", job["id"])
        if stored is not None and stored.get("rev", 0) != job.get("rev", 0):
            raise Stale(f"job {job['id']} changed since it was read "
                        f"(rev {job.get('rev', 0)}, now {stored.get('rev', 0)}); reload it")
        job["rev"] = job.get("rev", 0) + 1
        return _write(job)


def _write(job: dict) -> dict:
    job["updated"] = now()
    record = {k: v for k, v in job.items() if k != "constraints"}
    if "constraints" in job:
        snap = job["constraints"]
        # So a listing can tell, without reading every snapshot, which jobs read
        # their repository's own rules (lifecycle.project_catalogue).
        record["project_rules"] = records.has_project_rules(snap)
        job["project_rules"] = record["project_rules"]
        if _snapshots.get(job["id"]) != snap:
            backend.set("job-constraints", job["id"], snap)
            _snapshots[job["id"]] = json.loads(json.dumps(snap, default=str))
    backend.set("jobs", job["id"], record)
    return job


"""Oversight: how much a person is asked, checkpoint by checkpoint.

Governance is the gates and the feedback loops built into the factory: the
grant, the constraints, the checks failing first and then passing, the quality
gates, CI. Oversight is a control on it, not part of it: it decides only who
answers when the factory stops for a person, never whether a gate holds.
Observability and the audit record are the same at every level.

Each checkpoint has a dial:

- `ask`: stop and wait for a person (what the factory always did);
- `hold`: take the checkpoint's default answer after a window, unless a person
  answers first, and say so on the job while it waits;
- `auto`: take the default answer now.

A decision oversight takes is recorded as oversight's (actor `oversight`),
never as a person's, and a person can answer any checkpoint at any level while
it waits. Some checkpoints have a floor: the merge never goes below `hold`, so
a person is always told before code lands on the base branch.

Settings: `settings/oversight.yaml` (Settings page). A preset sets every
checkpoint; `checkpoints` and `repos.<name>` override it, never below a floor.
The preset is `high` unless the file says otherwise: everything asks.
"""

import config

LEVELS = ("ask", "hold", "auto")

# The checkpoints a person answers, by the `needs` kind the factory raises (and
# the merge, which is a person's action on a ready pull request), with the
# answer oversight takes for them, in words for the job's page.
CHECKPOINTS = {
    "questions": {"label": "Your answers", "default": "answer each question with its default"},
    "approve": {"label": "Your approval of the plan", "default": "approve the plan"},
    "checks": {"label": "Your acceptance tests", "default": "implement every proposed scenario"},
    "refused": {"label": "A refused call", "default": "retry, told what was refused and why"},
    "refactor": {"label": "Refactor", "default": "carry on without refactoring"},
    "review": {"label": "Review", "default": "carry on, recording the findings as declined"},
    "uat": {"label": "UAT", "default": "pass UAT, when the proof passed"},
    "merge": {"label": "Merge", "default": "merge, once CI is green", "floor": "hold"},
}

PRESETS = {
    "high": {k: "ask" for k in CHECKPOINTS},
    "medium": {"questions": "hold", "approve": "ask", "checks": "hold", "refused": "ask",
               "refactor": "hold", "review": "hold", "uat": "ask", "merge": "ask"},
    "low": {"questions": "auto", "approve": "hold", "checks": "auto", "refused": "hold",
            "refactor": "auto", "review": "auto", "uat": "hold", "merge": "hold"},
    "off": {**{k: "auto" for k in CHECKPOINTS}, "merge": "hold"},
}

WINDOW_MINUTES = 30


def settings() -> dict:
    found = config.read("oversight") if (config.SETTINGS / "oversight.yaml").is_file() else {}
    return found if isinstance(found, dict) else {}


"""wipp-factory: the thin factory, as an iii worker.

Three things are registered and nothing else:

* **`/wipp/*`**, observing the `http` worker's `http::on-request` — the app.
  One function per route; the route table, the identity check and the roles
  live in `api.py`.
* **`wipp::tick`**, observing the `cron` worker's `cron::on-tick` — the
  reconciler. Every few seconds it moves each unfinished job one step; see

* **`policy::check_permissions`** — the gate. wipp-harness calls it before

def save(job: dict) -> dict:
    """Write the job, unless it was written since this copy was read. Its
    constraint snapshot, if it carries one, is written apart, and only when it
    changed.

    Every write bumps `rev`, and a copy whose `rev` is not the stored one is
    refused (`Stale`). Without it the last writer won: a step that had read the
    job before a person pressed Stop wrote its copy back minutes later, and the
    job went on (docs/models/lifecycle.qnt, the `stopSticks` counterexample).
    """
    with _lock:
        stored = backend.get("jobs", job["id"])
        if stored is not None and stored.get("rev", 0) != job.get("rev", 0):
            raise Stale(f"job {job['id']} changed since it was read "
                        f"(rev {job.get('rev', 0)}, now {stored.get('rev', 0)}); reload it")
        job["rev"] = job.get("rev", 0) + 1
        return _write(job)


def _write(job: dict) -> dict:
    job["updated"] = now()
    record = {k: v for k, v in job.items() if k != "constraints"}
    if "constraints" in job:
        snap = job["constraints"]
        # So a listing can tell, without reading every snapshot, which jobs read
        # their repository's own rules (lifecycle.project_catalogue).
        record["project_rules"] = records.has_project_rules(snap)
        job["project_rules"] = record["project_rules"]
        if _snapshots.get(job["id"]) != snap:
            backend.set("job-constraints", job["id"], snap)
            _snapshots[job["id"]] = json.loads(json.dumps(snap, default=str))
    backend.set("jobs", job["id"], record)
    return job


"""Oversight: how much a person is asked, checkpoint by checkpoint.

Governance is the gates and the feedback loops built into the factory: the
grant, the constraints, the checks failing first and then passing, the quality
gates, CI. Oversight is a control on it, not part of it: it decides only who
answers when the factory stops for a person, never whether a gate holds.
Observability and the audit record are the same at every level.

Each checkpoint has a dial:

- `ask`: stop and wait for a person (what the factory always did);
- `hold`: take the checkpoint's default answer after a window, unless a person
  answers first, and say so on the job while it waits;
- `auto`: take the default answer now.

A decision oversight takes is recorded as oversight's (actor `oversight`),
never as a person's, and a person can answer any checkpoint at any level while
it waits. Some checkpoints have a floor: the merge never goes below `hold`, so
a person is always told before code lands on the base branch.

Settings: `settings/oversight.yaml` (Settings page). A preset sets every
checkpoint; `checkpoints` and `repos.<name>` override it, never below a floor.
The preset is `high` unless the file says otherwise: everything asks.
"""

import config

LEVELS = ("ask", "hold", "auto")

# The checkpoints a person answers, by the `needs` kind the factory raises (and
# the merge, which is a person's action on a ready pull request), with the
# answer oversight takes for them, in words for the job's page.
CHECKPOINTS = {
    "questions": {"label": "Your answers", "default": "answer each question with its default"},
    "approve": {"label": "Your approval of the plan", "default": "approve the plan"},
    "checks": {"label": "Your acceptance tests", "default": "implement every proposed scenario"},
    "refused": {"label": "A refused call", "default": "retry, told what was refused and why"},
    "refactor": {"label": "Refactor", "default": "carry on without refactoring"},
    "review": {"label": "Review", "default": "carry on, recording the findings as declined"},
    "uat": {"label": "UAT", "default": "pass UAT, when the proof passed"},
    "merge": {"label": "Merge", "default": "merge, once CI is green", "floor": "hold"},
}

PRESETS = {
    "high": {k: "ask" for k in CHECKPOINTS},
    "medium": {"questions": "hold", "approve": "ask", "checks": "hold", "refused": "ask",
               "refactor": "hold", "review": "hold", "uat": "ask", "merge": "ask"},
    "low": {"questions": "auto", "approve": "hold", "checks": "auto", "refused": "hold",
            "refactor": "auto", "review": "auto", "uat": "hold", "merge": "hold"},
    "off": {**{k: "auto" for k in CHECKPOINTS}, "merge": "hold"},
}

WINDOW_MINUTES = 30


def settings() -> dict:
    found = config.read("oversight") if (config.SETTINGS / "oversight.yaml").is_file() else {}
    return found if isinstance(found, dict) else {}

"""One shape for every harness: start a turn, ask how it is going, stop it.

Every harness composed here registers `<prefix>::start`, `::status` and
`::stop`. There is one, and it runs every turn in its job's sprite
(docs/sprite-execution-plan.md, S6): this machine holds every secret the
factory has, and no Claude process runs on it. A turn with no sprite to run in
is refused, never run here instead.

So each adapter declares its `confinement`, and only `strict` ones run unless
`settings/phases.yaml` says otherwise in so many words. Swapping models within a
harness is free; adding a harness is an adapter plus a test that its
confinement is what it claims.
"""

import os


import audit_client
import capabilities
import constraints
import gate
import partners
import prompt
import store

MCP_URL = os.environ.get("WIPP_MCP_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:3121/mcp")
SPRITE_TOOLS = [
    "mcp__wipp__sprite__exec",
    "mcp__wipp__sprite__code__read",
    "mcp__wipp__sprite__code__write",
    "mcp__wipp__sprite__code__list",
    "mcp__wipp__sprite__code__search",
    "mcp__wipp__sprite__code__tree",
    "mcp__wipp__sprite__code__glob",
]


# Off in the tests, whose stub trigger has no engine to list workers from; on in
# the running factory (factory.py turns it on at registration).
partners_checked = False


class Unavailable(RuntimeError):
    """This harness may not run here. Its message is the console's message."""


def scratch(job_id: str) -> str:
    """An empty directory to be the turn's cwd. Nothing in it, nothing to read."""
    path = store.DATA / "scratch" / job_id
    path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
"""A turn run in its job's sprite: the `sprite` harness (docs/sprite-execution-plan.md, S2).

The same three functions wipp-harness registers, under `wipp::sprite-turn::`,
so `harness.poll`, `harness.stop`, the Watch panel and the Turn page work as
they do for a turn on this machine. Nothing here runs Claude. The turn is
sprite-worker's (`sprite::agent::start / status / stop / remove`); this is wipp's
side of it: the broker's session (wipp's gate and audit, a secret per turn),
and the forwarder. Each poll asks for the turn's new `stream-json` events from
the offset kept here, and writes them as wipp-harness writes its own:
`agent::events` on the stream (the Watch panel) and `trace.step.*` on the
session log (the Turn page). The `result` event settles the record
`harness.poll` reads.

The turn's tool calls are the broker's (sprite-worker's agent/broker.py). The
broker asks the gate with each call exactly as the agent made it (the sprite
and the workspace are fixed, not named), so the Turn page pairs the steps
written here with their verdicts as they are.
A granted capability's call (`Skill`, `Task`, a remote MCP tool) is asked by
sprite-worker's hook through the broker, with its arguments as they are.
"""

import hashlib
import secrets

import forge
import gate
import store

PREFIX = "wipp::sprite-turn"
# How many times an interrupted turn (its sprite woke cold, say) is run again as
# the same Claude Code session before it counts as ended without a result.
RESUMES = 2
STREAM = "agent::events"
TOOL = "mcp__wipp__sprite__"


def functions_of(tools: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """`mcp__wipp__sprite__code__read` is the broker's `code::read`."""
    return [t.removeprefix(TOOL).replace("__", "::") for t in tools if t.startswith(TOOL)]

"""An agent in the sprite: Claude Code, run headless in a sprite, its tools served by a broker.

`sprite::agent::*`. Everything a caller needs to run a turn of Claude Code in
a sprite on a person's own token, with the agent unable to act except through
the tools this worker already offers, each put to the caller's policy first:

- `install`: the agent's runtime in a sprite, once, idempotently. Two users:
  the agent's (runs Claude Code; holds the token in its environment, nothing
  else) and an exec user (runs commands when a workspace has no container).
  Claude Code, pinned. Managed settings that leave the agent no tool but the
  broker's. The broker (`agent/broker.py`) and the code its tools are made of
  (this worker's own `code.py`, `paths.py`, `settings.py` and denylist),
  root-owned, as a sprite service.
- `policy`: the sprite's network policy, set from outside through the sprites
  API, and read-only inside.
- `start`, `status`, `stop`, `remove`: one turn. `start` writes the turn's files,
  its broker session (root-only, over stdin) and its token (root-only, over
  stdin, read into the runner's environment and deleted before Claude starts),
  then runs it as a sprite service. `status` reads the turn's `stream-json`
  events from an offset the caller keeps, so this worker holds no state.

What the caller decides: which tools a turn is granted, the policy and audit
endpoints the broker asks (and the secret and headers they need), the workspace
(a repository's container and non-root user, or the sprite), the MCP server's
name the tools appear under, and the network policy's rules.
"""

import hashlib
import io
import json
import re
import secrets
import shlex
import tarfile
from pathlib import Path

import cli
import settings

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
"""The agent's tools, in its sprite: sprite-worker's agent broker (`agent.py`).

A sprite service, run as root, installed by `sprite::agent::install` from this
directory and sprite-worker's own `code.py`, `paths.py` and `settings.py`, with
`container_cli.py` as their `cli`. The agent's Claude process (the agent user)
has no tool of its own; these are all it has.

For every call: the call is one of the session's granted tools, its command
passes the sprite denylist (`config/sprite.yaml`), the caller's policy endpoint
allows it (asked over HTTPS, failing closed), and only then does it run, in the
workspace (a repository's own container as a non-root user, or the sprite as
an unprivileged user). The result goes to the caller's audit endpoint, then to
the agent.

A call the agent's process makes itself, a capability the caller granted
(`Skill`, `Task`, a remote MCP server's tool), is not the broker's to run.
Claude Code's hook (`hook.py`, the only hook the managed settings allow) asks
here first, at `/hook`, and the broker puts it to the same policy.

Sessions are files written before each turn, root-only:
`<sessions>/<sha256 of the agent's secret>.json`, holding the session id, the
sprite and workspace, the granted tools, the MCP server's name, and the policy
and audit endpoints with their own secret (which the agent never holds) and
any headers they need. MCP over streamable HTTP, JSON responses, on 127.0.0.1.
"""

import hashlib
import json
import os
import sys

record (job, stage, grant, sprite, the constraints in force) before the turn
starts, so the first tool call already has something to be checked against.

`.constraints` log, the tick stops the turn, and a person decides what happens
next: give feedback and retry, allow that exact call once, or stop
(`stages.Factory.on_refused`).
